reasons: Claimed status is compliant and, consistent with that, the finding proposes no redline and no counterparty comment — the rendered paragraphs are identical to the originals.

The cited clause (§ 6.1) does bind our party (the Company/customer), so the rule is correctly treated as present rather than missing, and the direction analysis is right: the heavier two-year restriction in § 6.3 binds HDI (counterparty) and is properly not flagged.

The clause substantively meets the fallback on its material terms: scope is tied to a defined product set ('Deerskin Products', excluding closeout merchandise and Joan Cook Catalog items) plus named competitors, it applies 'during the term of this Agreement' only with no post-term tail on the Company, and the § 4.1 one-year term (renewing in one-year increments, terminable on 90 days' notice) keeps the effective duration within the 12-month cap.

No walk-away trigger is present — there is no post-term non-compete on the Company and the field of use is confined to Internet projects similar to the Site, leaving catalog/retail/sourcing activity unrestricted.

The two shortfalls versus the preferred position (elastic 'companies similar to' language and the absence of an internal-development/acquisition carve-out) are correctly noted in the rationale as sub-elements rather than escalated to a deviation, matching the playbook's classification semantics.
Deterministic check ('no open-ended compete restriction on Customer remains') passes and is consistent with the compliant classification.
